SUBJECT: Evening Echo - Registration Certificate be treated as "null and void"

The Evening Echo ( 大英晚報 ), an English language daily published in the evenings, at 6 Central Arcade, has ceased publication since the outbreak of the Pacific War in December 1941.

As the editor of the paper has failed to send back the registration certificate despite the repeated requests made by this Section, it is suggested that Registration Certificate No. C. 847 issued in respect of the paper be treated as "null and void".

FILE
G. Kennedy
Officer i/c Censorship Section.

Subject Evening Echo - Application for re-registration

Made by... D.S.I. Young Forwarded by... Supt. Mason

Forwarded herewith is an application by
Huang Shao-lai (黄少来), editor of the Evening
Echo for re-registration of the Evening Echo with
himself as editor.

The Evening Echo, a daily newspaper in English,
was first registered on 2.6.38 with Mr. L.L.F. Fearon
as Editor, Publisher and Proprietor. During its
period under his guidance nothing objectionable from
a police point of view has appeared in its pages
(see Registration No.F. 41 dated 10.6.38).

Huang Shao-lai, the new editor, is a native
of Fokien, aged 44. Between 1937 and 1938 he was
employed by the West Coast Life Insurance Co., 15
Canton Road. In the early part of 1939 he joined
the staff of the Evening Echo in the capacity of
assistant editor. He took over the post of editor
on 14.10.40 when Mr. Fearon sold the business to
the New China Publishing Co., 6 Central Arcade, of
which Lai Chiu-chi (黎智昭) is President. Mr. Lai
who also acts as publisher of the Evening Echo, is
a native of Canton, aged 38. He was last employed
by the Hongkong Daily Mail in Hongkong as Advertising
Manager for about five years, i.e. from 1933 to 1938.
He came to Shanghai three years ago and is unemployed
but lives on his private income.

Nothing to the detriment of the applicants
is known to this office.

事由 《大英晚报》——重新注册申请

由... 特别股督察 Young 制作 经由... 警司 Mason 转呈

现转呈《大英晚报》编辑黄少来（Huang Shao-lai）提出的重新注册《大英晚报》的申请，由其本人担任编辑。

《大英晚报》是一份英文日报，最初于1938年6月2日注册，当时 L.L.F. Fearon 先生担任编辑、发行人及业主。在他负责期间，该报未出现任何从警方角度看令人反感的内容（参见1938年6月10日的注册号 F. 41）。

新编辑黄少来，福建人，44岁。1937年至1938年间，他受雇于广东路15号的西海岸人寿保险公司。1939年初，他以助理编辑的身份加入《大英晚报》编辑部。1940年10月14日，当 Fearon 先生将业务出售给位于中央商场6号的新华出版公司时，他接任了编辑一职。该公司总裁为黎智昭（Lai Chiu-chi）。黎先生同时也担任《大英晚报》的发行人，他是广东人，38岁。他此前在香港《香港每日邮报》（Hongkong Daily Mail）担任广告经理约五年，即从1933年至1938年。他三年前来到上海，目前无业，靠私人收入生活。

本办公室未发现任何不利于申请人的情况。

REPORT
Date. Oct. 24, 1940.

Subject Shang Hai Siao Pao - Application for registration - Two
issues examined
Made by D.S.I. Young Forwarded by Supt. Mason

Reference instructions of D.C. (Special Branch)
appended to attached report of September 7, 1940,
Tsang Wen-tseng (章文正), editor and proprietor of
the Shang Hai Siao Pao (上海小報), a mosquito daily
in Chinese, was called to Headquarters on September 10,
when he was informed that registration would be
considered only after he had submitted to this office
copies of first seven issues for examination.

Two issues have been published, the first issue
being dated October 23. Perusal of these two issues
shows them to contain nothing objectionable from a
police point of view; but amongst other articles are
continuations from the Cycle Daily News (春秋日報),
a mosquito paper, House 441 Hankow Road, which ceased
publication on October 22 by order of the S.M. Police
(see Cycle Daily News file attached), of works of
fiction in serial form, including further installment
of the article in which the offending passages leading
to refusal of registration by the Police appeared,
but without any offensive matter included.

The first issue of the Shang Hai Siao Pao
also carried the following urgent notice inserted by
the Cycle Daily News:-

"Urgent Notice Issued by Cycle Daily News

"Acting on instructions from the Shanghai
Municipal Police, this paper has suspended
publication for the time being.
"All subscribers of this paper will be given
the Shang Hai Siao Pao instead of this paper."

D. C. (Crime and Special Branches).
D. S. I.
R. A. Young

REPORT

Subject Hai Mo (Bubble) - Application for registration

Made by D.S.I. Young Forwarded by Supt. Mason

Forwarded herewith is an application for
registration received from Chu Hsia-ching (朱夏卿),
editor and proprietor of the Hai Mo (Bubble 泡沫),
a semi-monthly magazine in Chinese, with offices at
14 Jehol Road.

Chu Hsia-ching, native of Ningpo, aged 24,
graduated in 1936 from the Kuo Kwang Middle School
(國光中学), then located at 619 Avenue Road. In
June 1937 he joined the Tsai Lun Tobacco Co.
(瑞倫烟公司), House 9 Lane 150 Kaifeng Road, where
he has worked as an accountant.

Fong Shing-pang (方兴邦), the publisher,
native of Kiangsu, aged 22, graduated in July 1939
from the Min Lih Middle School (民立中学), corner
of Yates and Weihaiwei Roads. In July of the same
year he went into the employ of the aforementioned
tobacco company as an apprentice.

Nothing to the detriment of the applicants
is known to this office.

The first issue appeared on October 15 and
second issue on November 1, 1940. Perusal of these
two issues (attached) shows them to contain prose
writings, translations from foreign publications,
reading matter on the life of university students and
short articles, in addition to advertisements of
commercial concerns, but nothing objectionable from
a police point of view.

with offices at 59 North Honan Road.

Huang Tah-jen, native of Kwangtung, aged 27,
is also known as Huang Kuo-shih (黄國光). He is
chief of the Secretariat of the Central China Daily
News (中華日報), principal propaganda organ of Wang
Ching-wei at 59 North Honan Road, registered with S.M.
Police under No.C. 521, which post he has held since
January 1940. Prior to this appointment, he studied
at the Shanghai University (滬江大學) in Yuen Ming
Yuen Road for one and a half years, namely from July
1938 to December 1939.

Nothing to his detriment is known to this
office.

that inserted by the Loh Yuan Tea Room (陸園茶室),
a gambling house located in Lane 1584 Chung Hwa Road,
West Gate, Nantao, but nothing objectionable from a
police point of view.

Applicant has been instructed to submit to
this office copies of two more issues for examination.

D. S. I.

事由：陈钟半月刊——注册申请

由副督察杨（Young）呈报，经警司梅森（Mason）转呈

现随文转呈一份注册申请，该申请来自黄达人（Huang Tah-jen），系中文杂志《晨钟半月刊》（Chen Chung Semi-monthly）的编辑、出版人及业主，办公地址位于河南路59号。

黄达人，广东籍，27岁，又名黄国光（Huang Kuo-shih）。他是位于河南路59号的《中华日报》（Central China Daily News，汪精卫的主要宣传机构）秘书处主任，该职位自1940年1月起担任，并在上海公共租界警务处以C. 521号注册。在此任命之前，他曾于圆明园路沪江大学（Shanghai University）就读一年半，即从1938年7月至1939年12月。

本局未掌握任何对其不利的资料。

第一期（附后）于1940年12月1日出版。经查阅，内容包含粤曲、图片及广告，其中包括位于南市西门中华路1584弄的赌窟陆园茶室（Loh Yuan Tea Room）刊登的广告，但从警务角度来看并无不当之处。

已指示申请人再提交两期样本供本局审查。

Reference instructions of P.A. to A.C. (Special
Branch) appended to attached report of October 24, 1940,
Sheh Hou-shih (石滬津), editor, publisher and
proprietor of the Pan Pih (半壁 ), a monthly magazine
in Chinese, was called to Headquarters on October 28
when he was informed that registration would be considered
only after he had submitted to this office draft of
first issue for examination.

November 12, 1940, perusal of which shows it to contain
for the most part translations of articles on international
problems appearing in foreign publications, in addition
to short articles, stories in serial form and
advertisements, but nothing objectionable from a police
point of view.

REPORT
Date. Oct. 24, 1940.

Subject Pan Pih - Application for registration

Made by D.S.I. Young Forwarded by Supt. Mason

Forwarded herewith is an application for
registration received from Sheh Hou-shih (石滬生),
editor, publisher and proprietor of the Pan Pih
(半壁 ), proposed monthly magazine in Chinese, with
offices at 620 Szechuen Road.

Sheh Hou-shih, native of Fokien, aged 32,
graduated in June 1935 from the Chi Chi University
(持志大学), then located in Kiangwan. In July 1935
he went into the employ of the Fan Foh Shing Import
& Export Co. (萬福興 ), then located in Museum Road,
where he worked as a member of the office staff until
August 1937 when the firm closed down as a result of
Sino-Japanese hostilities in Shanghai. In September
that year he secured a post in a similar capacity at
the Tien Yuan Co. (天源公司), an import and export
firm at 620 Szechuen Road, which post he still holds.

Nothing to his detriment is known to this
office.

The proposed monthly, according to the applicant,
will contain matter on general knowledge, literature,
biographies, international news and scientific knowledge,
in addition to advertisements of commercial firms.

D. S. I.
D. C. (Crime and Special Branches).

石沪生，福建籍，32岁，1935年6月毕业于位于江湾的持志大学（Chi Chi University）。1935年7月，他受雇于位于博物馆路的万福兴进出口公司（Fan Foh Shing Import & Export Co.），担任职员直至1937年8月，该公司因上海中日战事而停业。同年9月，他在四川路620号的进出口商行天源公司（Tien Yuan Co.）谋得类似职位，并至今仍在职。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.
Employees of the Chinese Press had quarrelled each other, subsequently a Japanese subject was involved.
At 9.30 a.m. on 22-4-43, C.P.W. 168 employed by the New Chinese Press (新中國報) 238 Hankow Road came to the station and reported that a quarrell occurred between the employees of the press and a Japanese subject inside at the of the Press Office. After a while, a Japanese subject named M. Hara (原正次) business manager of the Mainichi Daiben Co. (每日代辦公司) Room 301, 668 Szechuen Road, came to the station and reported that his junior staff named I. Mine (峯郁也), staff of the said firm and a Chinese messenger boy named Chang Wen Tsung (張文正), 22, Shanghai, were locked up in the New China Press Office..
D.P.S. I. Asakawa and C.P.S. 178 attended the scene and brought all concerned to the station.

调查记录。
《新中国报》员工发生争吵，随后一名日本籍人士卷入其中。
1943年4月22日上午9时30分，受雇于汉口路238号《新中国报》（New Chinese Press）的华捕168号来到捕房报告，称报社员工与一名日本籍人士在报社办公室内发生争吵。过了一会儿，一名名为原正次（M. Hara）的日本籍人士，系四川路668号301室每日代办公司（Mainichi Daiben Co.）的业务经理，来到捕房报告，称其下属职员峯郁也（I. Mine），即该公司职员，以及一名22岁的上海籍华人信差张文正（Chang Wen Tsung），被锁在《新中国报》办公室内。

native of...Shanghai, ........................................taken by me....................................................

Tang Yung Tsung, 28, nativ. of Shanghai, residing at 738 Thor-
burn Road, states as follows:-

I am employed by the Kuh Ts Wei Zeu(合資会社每日代弁所).

At about 9a.m. 22-4-43(Thursday) I was instructed to fetch one
China Weekly Newspaper dated 28-3-43. I then used one of our com-
pany's bicycle to proceed to the above newspaper office and on
arriving there I parked the machine outside the rear door of the
said newspaper concern, because on each occasion I had to communi-
cate with Mr. Kao Zang Kung of the Advertising Dept. first. At
that juncture, someone warned me not to place any bicycle there.
When I was pulling my bicycle, the man in question scolded me and
I asked him regarding the reason as to why he scolded me, but he
instead of answering my question struck me. At the same time, there
appeared one man wearing foreign dress(known to be one named Chu)
and struck my face once. I then asked him (Chu) as why he struck
me, he ordered some printing workers and watchman to pull me inside
the door where I was seriously assaulted by them. Later Mr. Kao
handed over to me the China Weekly and I intended to leave the
newspaper office but I found that both the front and back were
closed. I then talked to the watchman who again struck and kicked
me. Shortly afterwards, there appeared four or five men wearing
uniform and they joined the former 5 or 6 men assaulting me again.
After that I was allowed to go and when I return to my firm I re-
ported the matter to manager Mr. Morishita. I was then accompanied
by Mr. Mine to go to the China Weekly Newspaper Coy. and asked why
I was assaulted, but all the employees ignored the question. Mr. Mi-
ne then asked me who were the men assaulting me and I then pointed

唐永宗（Tang Yung Tsung，注：此处英文名与前文拼音不符，依原文译出），28岁，上海籍，居住于韬宾路738号，陈述如下：-

我受雇于合资会社每日代辩所（Kuh Ts Wei Zeu）。

1943年4月22日（星期四）上午9点左右，我奉命去取一份日期为1943年3月28日的《中国周报》。随后我使用公司的一辆自行车前往上述报社，到达后将车停在该报社后门外面，因为每次我都必须先与广告部的高藏公（Kao Zang Kung，音译）先生联系。就在那时，有人警告我不要在那里停放自行车。当我正在拉自行车时，那个人骂我，我问他为什么骂我，但他没有回答我的问题，反而打了我。同时，出现了一个穿西装的人（已知姓朱），打了我脸部一下。于是我问他（朱）为什么打我，他命令一些印刷工人和巡捕把我拉进门内，我在那里遭到他们的严重殴打。后来高先生把《中国周报》交给我，我打算离开报社，但发现前后门都关着。我便与巡捕交谈，他又打我又踢我。不久，出现了四五个穿制服的人，他们加入了之前的五六个人再次殴打我。之后我被允许离开，回到公司后我向经理森下先生报告了此事。随后由峯先生陪同我去《中国周报》公司询问为何遭殴打，但所有员工都无视这个问题。于是峯先生问我谁是殴打我的人，我便指出

pages.en:
"2"
out the watchman who intended to deny. Mr. Mine then showed injuries
on my face to the watchman. Mr. Mine was then smoking a cigarette
and he inadvertently touched the watchman's face, the latter es-
caped to the upstairs room. However, Mr. Mine followed him to the
upstairs room where he again entered into an inner room. Then I
and Mr. Mine came downstairs and discovered that both the front and
back doors were closed and locked again. We waited for about
half an hour and we asked the employees to open the door but
none of them would comply with the request. I then tested my
own key and succeeded in opening the lock. We then telephoned
to our manager who was already making a report in the Police
Station regarding the illegal detention by the newspaper em-
ployees. I together with Mr. Mine walked a while and Mr. Mine
departed with me as he had some important business. I then re-
turned to our firm and on instructions of Mr. Morishita I went
to the newspaper office again and on arriving there I saw a
Japanese Detective, a Chinese detective and Mr. Morishita there.
Later I together with three employees of the newspaper office and
myself attended the Central Police Station.
The above is my true statement.

Signed:-

“2”
出去找那个打算抵赖的守夜人。Mine 先生随后向守夜人展示了我脸上的伤痕。当时 Mine 先生正吸着香烟，他不慎触碰到了守夜人的脸，后者逃到了楼上的房间。然而，Mine 先生跟着他到了楼上房间，他又进入了一个内室。随后我和 Mine 先生下楼，发现前后门都再次被关上并锁住了。我们等了大约半小时，要求雇员开门，但无人听从。于是我试了自己的钥匙，成功打开了锁。随后我们打电话给我们的经理，他已经在警察局就报社雇员非法拘禁一事进行报案。我和 Mine 先生走了一会儿，因有要事，Mine 先生与我一同离开。随后我返回我们公司，按照 Morishita 先生的指示，我再次前往报社办公室，到达那里时，我看到一名日本侦探、一名中国侦探和 Morishita 先生在那里。后来，我与报社的三名员工一起前往中央捕房。
以上是我的真实陈述。

Kou Chia Chung (顾家钟), 25, Tsangchow, residing at 112 South Jen

This morning at 9 o'clock, in front of our Newspaper Office,
one person, ridden on a bicycle, left the machine just accrossed
the entrance door, then I asked him to put aside, he started to
scold and beat me. As some people on the street came up in order
to make us peaceful. He also beat them. Afterwards, this person
with a Japanese came to our Office and closed the door first, then
began to beat and threw away chairs, desks, and disordered the
Office. Then they opened the door and went away.

| | Chu Yao Tung (朱耀東), 37, Haichow, residing at 38 Foh Lai Road states as follows:- |
| :--- | :--- |
| | At 9a.m. this morning, I came to the newspaper office, and saw one named Chang Wan Tsung (張文正), newspaper coolie, put his bicycle accrossed the rear entrance door. Then Kou Chin Chung (顧新中) asked him to put it aside, but he will not put it away, then they quarrelled and fought with each other at last. Then I advised the Chang to go away but he will not later I asked him to go inside. I myself go to the office and asked another newspaper deliverer named Koo Chang King (高長根) to send out the Chang. When he was going out he was still scolding. About half hour later, Chang came back again with two Japanese, one stand at outside and one come inside with an angry face. First of all, the Japanese used his cigarette hurt the watchman's face (王岐山) and again go to the office and beat anyone he met. He threw away chairs and face-bowl. Again he go to upstairs and awaked another two persons who slept there. Because I saw that he was still very angry and I can not speak to him, I ask the watchman to report the Police Station. Signed. |

（印：清道）

Date: April 11, 1940.
REPORT
Subject. Ta Lei Wan Pao - Statement of ownership
Made by. D. S. I. Golder Forwarded by. Supt. Mason

Forwarded herewith is a statement of
ownership by the President of the Evening Post and
Mercury contained in the December 16, 1937, issue of
that paper referring in positive terms to the exact
ownership of the Ta Lei Wan Pao.
Mr. Randall Gould is the editor of the Ta
Lei Wan Pao and there is no doubt that the paper is
entirely American owned.
It will be noted that no reference is made to
the Ta kei Pao, also published by the Mercury Press,
and of which Mr. Randall Gould is editor. This
paper appeared much later than the Ta Mei Wan Pao
and is believed to be owned largely by Chinese
interests although proof of this is lacking.

D. C. (Special Branch).

pages.en:
The Youth Semi-Monthly (青年大衆), vol.2, Issue No. 1,
dated August 5, 1939 :-

A BOATMAN

Rifle firing was heard coming from the village
ahead. The people became panic-stricken.
Subsequently, some ten short invaders were noticed
arriving in a hurried manner. They were in an embarrassing
condition. Some of them had been wounded and it shows
that they had been defeated at the front.
They jumped upon a small boat on the small creek.
One of the soldiers dragged out an old man sleeping in the
bottom of the boat and said to him: "Are you a guerrilla?"
The old man was trembling and it seemed that he did not
understand what the soldier said.
Another said: "I tell you. Quickly row the
boat to the city."
Before the bright rifles and bayonets, the old
man was so frightened that he could not speak.
"Will you go" said one of the soldiers who took
his rifle in the hand and pointed it to the breast of the
old man.
"Sir, I am so old that I cannot row the boat"
replied the old man.
The soldier became angry and assaulted the old man.
"You go or refuse to go", he said in a violent
voice.
"I go, I go" said the old man who went to the
rear side of the boat and began to row the boat.
Suddenly the old man jumped into the water and
overturned the boat, whereupon all on board were thrown
into the water.
The old man struck all in the water with his oars
pages.zh:
《青年大众》（The Youth Semi-Monthly），第2卷，第1期，
日期：1939年8月5日：-

船夫

前方村庄传来了步枪射击声。人们惊慌失措。
随后，大约十名身材矮小的入侵者匆忙赶到。他们处境狼狈。其中一些人受了伤，这表明他们在前线战败了。
他们跳上小溪里的一艘小船。一名士兵把睡在船底的一位老人拖出来，对他说：“你是游击队吗？”
老人浑身发抖，似乎听不懂士兵的话。
另一人说：“我告诉你。快把船划到城里去。”
在明亮的刺刀和步枪面前，老人吓得说不出话来。
“你走不走？”一名士兵手里拿着步枪，枪口指着老人的胸口说道。
“先生，我太老了，划不动船，”老人回答道。
士兵大怒，殴打了老人。
“你到底走还是不走，”他用凶狠的声音说道。
“我走，我走，”老人说着走到船尾，开始划船。
突然，老人跳入水中，弄翻了小船，船上的人全都掉进了水里。
老人用船桨击打水中所有的人

pages.en:
(2)

and made them to drink water a great deal if possible.
"Are you successful, Lord Wong" said some 4 or 5
young men, who stood up from the reeds with rifles in their
hands.
"If there were a double number of the men, I,
an old man, would still be able to deal with them," replied
the old man.
The moon was shining. On the surface of the
creek, some ten corpses were seen floating before the night
wind.
The old man laughed on the shore.

------
pages.zh:
(2)

并尽可能让他们喝个饱。
“黄老爷，成功了吗？”四五名手持步枪、从芦苇丛中站起来的年轻人问道。
“就算人数再多一倍，我这个老头子也能对付他们，”老人回答道。
月光照耀着。在小溪的水面上，可以看到大约十具尸体在夜风中漂浮。
老人在岸上大笑。

------

Subject. Objectionable article appearing in the "Youth Semi-monthly"
on April 5, 1939.
Made by. and Forwarded by. C.D.I. Ross.

With reference to the attached anti-Japanese
article published in the "Youth Semi-monthly" (青年大衆),
a Chinese language magazine, 16, Lane 145, Kuling Road,
of April 5, Mr. Tsang Yi-vai (張依凡), the editor
of the magazine, was interviewed at headquarters on
May 5, when he was warned that the publication of
articles of this nature was highly undesirable and that
a repetition of the offence would result in the
withdrawal of the registration certificate issued to
the magazine.

Mr. Tsang expressed his regret and promised
to observe these instructions.

FILED
C. D. I.

"The Youth Semi-monthly"(青年大衆) published the following
article on April 5, 1939:-

One cold and dark winter night,
a meeting was held by 34 farmers in a house in King
Ka Village(金家村) in an occupied area. A man named
Ts Ping(志平) acted as Chairman. The Chairman
announced that ghosts would come to oppress them if
they did not pay their taxes.

One of the farmers cursed and said:-
"Since their invasion of our country, they have plundered,
slaughtered, raped and committed other acts of violence.
After the inauguration of the Maintenance Association,
all kinds of taxation have been imposed upon us. They want
our lives."

At last, one of them proposed
joining the mobile unit. To this all agreed. The
following slogans were then shouted:-
"Long live our leader!"
"Long live China!"
"Down with the Japanese ghosts!"
"Down with the high-nosed Chen Ma
Bee(陳麻皮) (the Chief of the
Maintenance Association)!"

《青年大众》于1939年4月5日刊登了以下文章：-

在一个寒冷黑暗的冬夜，
34名农民在被占领区金家村（King Ka Village）的一户人家中举行会议。一名叫志平（Ts Ping）的人担任主席。主席宣布，如果他们不缴纳税款，鬼魂就会来压迫他们。

一名农民咒骂道：-
“自从他们入侵我国以来，他们抢劫、屠杀、强奸并犯下其他暴行。在‘大道政府’成立后，各种税收强加于我们身上。他们想要我们的命。”

最后，其中一人提议加入流动部队。所有人都同意了。随后高呼以下口号：-
“领袖万岁！”
“中国万岁！”
“打倒日本鬼子！”
“打倒高鼻子的陈麻皮（Chen Ma Bee）（‘大道政府’首领）！”

Made by ............ and ............ Forwarded by D.S. McKeown.

Attached is an application for the registration of
the "Tsung Seh Pictorial Semi-monthly" (春色畫画半月刊),
No. 4, Lane 153, Carter Road.
Tu Zung-tsoong (屠承忠), the proprietor and
publisher, is an accountant in the employ of the local office
of the Yangchow Flour Mill, 96 Avenue Road. He published
a ten-day periodical entitled "Hsun Pao" (旬報)(Registration
certificate No. C.161) in May this year but this publication
closed down in July.
Sung Zei (沈邃), the editor, is an employee of the
Foh I.i Trading Company (福利實業公司), 406 Kiangse Road.
The "Tsung Seh" Pictorial was formerly published by
the Chien Chiu (千秋) Publishing Company, No. 4, Lane 153,
Carter Road, of which Tu Zung-tsoong was an employee and one
Zung Foo-wo (陳富華) the manager. On May 5, 1937 Zung Foo-wo
was fined $30 by the Shanghai 1st Special District Court for
publishing indecent pictures in the magazine. It is said
that the Chien Chiu Publishing Company has ceased operations
and that Zung Foo-wo has no longer any connection with the
"Tsung Seh" magazine.

D.C. (Special Branch).    J.M. Brown
                          D. S.

Subject (in full) Modern Children - Editor interviewed

Made by D.S.I. Golder Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

The Modern Children (現代兒童), a weekly
magazine registered with the S.M.C. on November 3, 1938,
under No.C. 324 ceased publication in July, 1939.
On March 5, Yi Fei-yuan (美飛鶯), the editor
of the magazine, was interviewed at Headquarters and
asked to return the certificate issued in respect of his
publication. On presenting the certificate, the editor
stated that the magazine would probably resume
publication some time next month.
It is therefore respectfully suggested that
the certificate (attached) be filed, pending definite
indication from the editor that the magazine will again
start operations.

Made by D.S.I. Young Forwarded by Supt. Mason

The Ta Chung News Agency (大众通訊社), Room
501 Tse Shu Building, Nanking Road, registered with
S.M. Police under No.C. 332 ceased functioning recently.
Enquiries show that the offices of the news
agency have been vacated, present whereabouts of Wu
Dah (吴达), editor, publisher and proprietor, being
unknown.
It is therefore suggested that certificate
No.C. 332, the return of which cannot be effected, be
declared "null and void."

Cancel registration

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. B. REGISTRY File No. 8/6-9-C left By D. S. P. Station, Date 27 April 23, 1940.）

REPORT

Subject Crystal - Prosecution of A.L. Teodoro, publisher, in U.S.
Court for China

Made by. D.S. Pharazyn Forwarded by. Supt. Mason

With reference to the attached, A.L. Teodoro,
publisher of the Crystal, Chinese mosquito daily,
was arrested by Mr. Peterson, assistant U.S. Marshal
for China, on 22.4.40 and detained in Central
Station overnight.

On 23.4.40 Teodoro was brought before the
U.S. Court for China, Development Building, and
charged by Mr. Leighton Shields, District Attorney,
on four counts of publishing indecent, obscene and
lascivious articles. Teodoro pleaded guilty
and police witnesses were not required. He was
sentenced by Judge Milton J. Helmick to a fine of
U.S. $10 on the first count and to a term of
imprisonment of 10 months in Bilibid Prison, Manila,
on the other three counts, the latter sentence to
be suspended for 5 years, he being placed on parole
for that period. In the event of his contravening
the law during that time he may be arrested by the
U.S. Marshal and sent to Manila to serve his sentence.

Teodoro paid the fine and has now been
released.

（印：INDEXED BY (S.B.) REGISTRY DATE 27/4/40）

D. S. Pharazyn
D. C. (Special Branch).

主题 Crystal（《水晶报》）- 在美国驻华法院起诉出版人 A.L. 特奥多罗 (Teodoro)

关于附件事宜，《Crystal》（一家中文小型日报）的出版人 A.L. 特奥多罗 (A.L. Teodoro) 于1940年4月22日被美国驻华副法警彼得森 (Peterson) 先生逮捕，并在中央捕房拘留过夜。

1940年4月23日，特奥多罗被提审至发展大楼的美国驻华法院，由地区检察官莱顿·希尔兹 (Leighton Shields) 先生以四项刊登淫秽、猥亵及色情文章的罪名提出指控。特奥多罗认罪，故无需警方证人出庭。法官米尔顿·J·赫尔米克 (Milton J. Helmick) 判处其在第一项罪名上罚款10美元，在其他三项罪名上判处在马尼拉比利比德监狱 (Bilibid Prison) 监禁10个月，后一项刑期缓刑5年，在此期间将其置于假释状态。若在此期间其违反法律，美国法警可将其逮捕并送往马尼拉服刑。

特奥多罗已缴纳罚款，现已获释。

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.
APR 23 1940
A. Teodoro Sentenced In US Court
Paper Publishes
Lewd Articles
Jail Term Suspended
Five Years; Fine
Imposed
Pleading guilty to all charges
Mr. A. Teodoro publisher of the
"Crystal" who was arrested yes-
terday, was given a suspended
sentence of six months in Bilibid
Prison, Manila, warned to be
prudent in his work and fined
US$10 by Judge Milton J. Hel-
mick in the United States Court
for China this morning.
Mr. A. Teodoro was arrested fol-
lowing the publication of several
indecent articles expressed in the
Chinese language daily.
Warned
Prior to his arrest yesterday
Mr. Teodoro was warned on
November 14, 1939 to cease pub-
lishing articles of lewd and inde-
cent nature in his magazine the
"Crystal," the court was informed
today.
This warning, however, was
disregarded by Mr. Teodoro, who
subsequently allowed articles and
stories of the same nature to ap-
pear in print on February, 17, 18
and 22, 1940, respectively.
Arrested
Mr. Leighten Shields, District
Attorney for the United States
Court for China, subsequently
made out a warrant for his arrest.
This was carried out yesterday.
Bail of US$200 was asked, but
the publisher, unable to produce
the money, was sent to Ward Road
prison to await trial which took
place this morning.
"Stick To Cigars"
Judge Milton J. Helmick during
the hearing today suggested to the
prisoner "Don't you think it is
better to stick to cigars?" To
which the prisoner answered that
it was "not such a profitable line."
Leniency for Mr. Teodoro was
asked by the District Attorney,
who suggested that six months
suspended sentence be given to
him. The judgement followed the
suggestion. The suspension period
is five years.
Pleading guilty, the prisoner
also said that he did not know
that these articles were against
the law.

A. 特奥多罗在美国法院被判刑
报纸刊登
淫秽文章
监禁刑期缓刑
五年；处以
罚款
对所有指控认罪
《Crystal》出版人 A. 特奥多罗先生昨日被捕，今晨在美国驻华法院被法官米尔顿·J·赫尔米克判处在马尼拉比利比德监狱监禁六个月（缓刑），警告其在工作中要谨慎行事，并罚款10美元。
A. 特奥多罗先生是在其中文日报刊登数篇不雅文章后被捕的。
警告
法庭今日获悉，特奥多罗先生在昨日被捕前，曾于一九三九年十一月十四日受到警告，要求其停止在杂志《Crystal》中刊登淫秽和不雅性质的文章。
然而，特奥多罗先生无视这一警告，随后允许同类性质的文章和故事分别于一九四零年二月十七日、十八日和二十二日见报。
逮捕
美国驻华法院地区检察官莱顿·希尔兹 (Leighten Shields) 先生随后签发了逮捕令。该逮捕令于昨日执行。保释金要求为200美元，但因出版人无法拿出这笔钱，他被送往华德路监狱等待今晨进行的审判。
“坚持做雪茄生意”
法官米尔顿·J·赫尔米克在今日的听证会上向囚犯建议：“你不认为坚持做雪茄生意更好吗？”囚犯回答说那“不是那么有利可图的行当”。
地区检察官请求对特奥多罗先生从宽处理，建议给予其六个月缓刑。判决采纳了这一建议。缓刑期为五年。
囚犯在认罪时还表示，他不知道这些文章是违法的。

US Court Seizes
Paper Publisher
Language In Chinese
Journal Found
Indecent
Mr. Andres L. Teodoro, Filipino,
was arrested this morning by the
United States Marshal for China
for allowing the publication of
alleged indecent and lewd articles
in Chinese to appear in his
magazine, the Crystal.
Asked to furnish a bond of
US$200, the prisoner was unable
to do so and thereupon was sent
to the Ward Road jail, for deten-
tion.
Lascivious Language
Published by the Chinese and
American Union Company, under
which name Mr. Teodoro was
doing business, the magazine had
several times printed stories in
the Chinese language which were
written in language, which is
alleged now to have been lasci-
vious.
Under American law, the ar-
rested man faces a charge which
may bring a prison term in Shang-
hai if he is found guilty by the
United States Court for China.
Case Coming Up
He also faces a charge of having
in possession, to sell and exhibit
a certain pamphlet entitled "The
Crystal," published in the Chin-
ese language.
Mr. Leighton Shields, District
Attorney for the United States
Court in China, will prosecute.
The case will be heard in the
Court in a short while. Mean-
while the prisoner has been sent
to the Ward Road prison to await
trial.

1940年4月22日
美国法院查封
报刊出版人
中文刊物
被指淫秽

菲律宾籍男子安德烈斯·L·特奥多罗（Andres L. Teodoro）先生，今晨被驻华美国法警逮捕，理由是其允许在其杂志《晶报》（The Crystal）上刊登据称淫秽和下流的中文文章。

被告被要求提供200美元保释金，但无力支付，随即被送往华德路监狱羁押。

淫秽语言

该杂志由中美联合公司（Chinese and American Union Company）出版，特奥多罗先生以该公司名义经营。该杂志曾多次刊登中文故事，其行文据称现被认定为淫秽。

根据美国法律，若被驻华美国法院判定有罪，被捕者将面临可能在上海服刑的指控。

案件即将审理

他还面临一项指控，即持有、意图出售及展示一本名为《晶报》的中文小册子。

驻华美国法院地区检察官莱顿·希尔兹（Leighton Shields）先生将提起公诉。
该案将于不久后在法院开庭审理。与此同时，囚犯已被送往华德路监狱候审。

"Crystal" (晶報), a mosquito newspaper, published the
following article on April 15, 1940 :-

VIOLATION OF COMMANDMENTS AGAINST WINE AND LASCIVIOUSNESS

In Tien Shiang Yuan (天香院), there lived a dark
faced and corpulent girl by the name of Feng Kuei (鳳葵). One
day she felt depressed. As she had nothing to do, she left
the house. On the way she met a drunkard. Snatching from
his hands a bottle of high class brandy she drank it all. She
later walked into a wine shop in the village and ordered some
wine and food. At that time there were several other people
in the shop all of whom were fierce looking and were probably
highwaymen.

The waiter asked the girl to keep the men company
to which the girl agreed. At first she and the so-called
leader drank 10 bowls of wine each. Soon the leader became
heavily drunk and began to vomit. The girl drank 10 more
bowls of wine and ate all the food on the table, after which
she left the shop.

As the wine she had drunk was beginning to take
effect, she halted, intending to take a rest under a tree.
Suddenly she heard a clamour some distance away. Looking
out she saw 7 or 8 children chasing after a dog and a bitch
which were engaged in the sexual act. The sight angered the
girl. She said, "How dare you two beasts violate the rules
of our Tien Shiang Yuan which prohibit any contact with the
male sex? How dare you secretly indulge in a lascivious act
here?"

Saying this, she unknotted a band from her waist
and tied it around the connected genitals of the two animals
and dragged them to the Tien Shiang Yuan.

On arrival she found that the two animals were
already dead although they were still linked together. She
broke into a hysterical laugh which attracted all the girl

《晶报》（Crystal），一份小型八卦报纸，于1940年4月15日刊登了以下文章：

违反戒酒与戒淫之戒律

在天香院（Tien Shiang Yuan），住着一个面色黝黑、身材肥胖的女孩，名叫凤葵（Feng Kuei）。一天，她感到郁闷。因无事可做，便离家外出。途中遇到一个醉汉。她从醉汉手中抢过一瓶高档白兰地，一饮而尽。随后她走进村里的一家酒馆，点了一些酒菜。当时店里还有几个人，个个面目凶狠，可能是强盗。

侍者要求女孩陪那些男人喝酒，女孩答应了。起初，她和那个所谓的头目各喝了十碗酒。不久，头目酩酊大醉，开始呕吐。女孩又喝了十碗酒，吃光了桌上的食物，然后离开了酒馆。

由于喝下的酒开始发作，她停下脚步，打算在树下休息。突然，她听到远处一阵喧闹。放眼望去，看见七八个孩子正在追赶一只公狗和一只母狗，它们正在进行交配。这一幕激怒了女孩。她说：“你们这两只畜生，怎敢违反我们天香院禁止与雄性接触的规定？怎敢在此偷偷行淫？”

说着，她解开腰间的带子，绑在两只动物相连的生殖器上，将它们拖到了天香院。

到达时，她发现两只动物虽然仍连在一起，但已经死亡。她发出一阵歇斯底里的笑声，吸引了天香院所有的女

Feng Kuei had become strong after the drinks.

January 24, 1940. Afternoon Translation.

Hwa Pao and National Herald :-
WANG CHING-WEI'S FOLLOWERS ADVISED TO REPENT.

The Anti-Corruption Movement Committee of various circles in Shanghai yesterday addressed a letter to Wang Ching-wei's followers pursuading them to repent and to accept this as a last advice. The letter stated that although Wang Ching-wei had despatched a circular telegram supporting the policy of Hirota and the statement of Konoye, the people in Shanghai have paid no heed to him.

Wang Ching-wei fully understands that Japan will never give up her original policy. He intends to promote his peace movement in order to disrupt the unity of China and to lower her spirit in the war of resistance.

Recently Wang signed with Japan a pact, which is more harmful than the Twenty-one Demands, for the formation of a new puppet government. Wang's plans have been completely exposed and it is hoped that members of his organisation will quickly return to the righteous path.

劝汪精卫追随者悔悟。

汪精卫充分理解日本绝不会放弃其原有政策。他意图推动其和平运动，以破坏中国的团结，并削弱其抗战精神。

January 24, 1940. Afternoon Translation.

Chinese-American Daily News, Ta Mei Pao, Sin Wan Pao, Shun
Pao, National Herald, Hwa Pao (Chungking telegram) :-

GENERAL CHIANG KAI-SHEK ISSUES OPEN LETTER TO PEOPLE ON
SECRET PACT CONCLUDED BETWEEN WANG CHING-WEI AND JAPAN

General Chiang Kai-shek has issued the
following open letter addressed to the people throughout
the country on the secret pact concluded between Wang Ching-
wei and Japan:-

Recently, Chinese and foreign newspapers
published a humiliating document known as the "Principles
for the readjustment of new relations between Japan and
China" which Wang Ching-wei and the Japanese had concluded
in Shanghai and was taken to Tokyo by Inouki with
the conditions submitted by Wang Ching-wei to the Japanese
for the creation of a puppet regime, and the reply from the
Japanese.

I am sure that the people throughout the .
country, after reading these documents, will have gained a
deeper insight into the treacherous schemes of the Japanese
and Wang Ching-wei; Through the revelations made by these
documents we can now understand the underhand activities
between the Japanese and the puppet authorities during the
past few months and the results of the discussions held by
the Japanese Asia Development Board a month ago. Before these
documents were published, we were already convinced that
Wang Ching-wei would unhesitatingly barter away the whole
nation and the life of China's future generations.

I want the people to study these documents
carefully and then to read my speech of December, 1938,
denouncing Prince Konoye's statement. A comparison between
the "Principles for the readjustment of new relations between
Japan and China" and Prince Konoye's statement will prove
that my criticisms made a year ago are correct. I declared
at that time that Japan's real desire was to annex the whole
of China and to annihilate the Chinese people and that Prince
Konoye's statement was an admission of Japan's ambition to
dominate East Asia and then to conquer the world. To-day
my words have been proved to be correct. The "Principles for
the readjustment of new relations between Japan and China"
gives definite shape to Prince Konoye's statement.

This pact between Japan and the puppet, . . .
authorities is ten times more severe than the 21 Demands . .
and even harsher than the measures adopted by Japan to
enslave Korea. I firmly believe that all righteous-minded
Chinese people cannot help being infuriated upon reading
such a document.

During the past year Wang Ching-wei has been
shamelessly propagating a peace which, he states, will not
harm China's independence or liberty; he has also been
clamouring for "good relations with neighbouring countries,"
a "common front against communism" and "an economic rapprochement".
From the pact concluded between Wang Ching-wei and the
Japanese, we can understand the significance of these three
expressions which, for the benefit of the people, I shall
put briefly as follows:-

The so-called "good relations with neighbouring
countries" means the incorporation of China with Japan."
The "common front against communism" is tantamount to the
maintaining of a perpetual garrison in China by Japan. The

《中美日报》、《大美晚报》、《新闻报》、《申报》、《国民公报》、《华报》（重庆电）：-

蒋介石将军就汪精卫与日本缔结的秘密协定向民众发表公开信

蒋介石将军就汪精卫与日本缔结的秘密协定，向全国民众发表了如下公开信：-

近日，中外报纸刊登了一份名为《调整中日新关系原则》的屈辱性文件，该文件系汪精卫与日本人在上海达成，由井木（Inouki，音译）带往东京，内容包括汪精卫为建立傀儡政权向日本人提出的条件以及日本人的答复。

我相信，全国民众在阅读这些文件后，将对日本人和汪精卫的奸诈阴谋有更深刻的认识。通过这些文件的披露，我们现在可以了解过去几个月里日本人与傀儡当局之间的幕后活动，以及一个月前日本东亚发展委员会（Asia Development Board，原文如此，通常指“兴亚院”或类似机构）举行讨论的结果。在这些文件公布之前，我们就已确信，汪精卫会毫不犹豫地出卖整个国家及中国子孙后代的生计。

我希望民众仔细研究这些文件，然后阅读我于1938年12月谴责近卫亲王声明的演讲。将《调整中日新关系原则》与近卫亲王的声明进行比较，将证明我一年前的批评是正确的。我当时宣称，日本的真正欲望是吞并整个中国并消灭中国人民，而近卫亲王的声明承认了日本统治东亚进而征服世界的野心。今天，我的话已被证明是正确的。《调整中日新关系原则》使近卫亲王的声明具体化。

日本与傀儡当局之间的这项协定，比“二十一条”苛刻十倍……甚至比日本奴役朝鲜所采取的措施更为严酷。我坚信，所有有良知的中国人在阅读这样一份文件时，无不感到愤怒。

在过去的一年里，汪精卫一直无耻地宣扬一种他声称不会损害中国独立或自由的“和平”；他还一直叫嚷“善邻友好”、“共同防共”和“经济提携”。从汪精卫与日本人缔结的协定中，我们可以理解这三个表述的含义，为了民众的利益，我将简要概括如下：-

所谓的“善邻友好”意味着将中国与日本合并。“共同防共”等同于日本在中国永久驻军。

expression "economic rapprochement" is nothing less than
the economic domination of China by Japan. This is what
Japan expects after Wang Ching-wei has enslaved China.
I have no desire to elucidate one by one all
the harsh terms contained in the pact; I will, however,
deal with some of the more important points. Firstly, let
us examine some of the main points:-
(1) Under the theory of "constructing a New
Order in East Asia" and "good relations with neighbouring
countries," it is intended to bring about rapprochement
among Japan, China and Manchukuo. The day that such a
rapprochement is effected will see an end to the indepen-
dence of our country.
(2) It is proposed to demark North China and
Mongolia as a region for a strong union of national defence
and economic affairs and the creation of a special military
and political status in Mongolia. Now, let me ask, whose
national defence is meant by this so-called national defence?
Can China be called an independent country when she has to
create a special status in her own territory for the
co-operation with Japan in the matter of national defence?
(3) The creation of a region in the Lower Yangtze
for close economic co-operation simply means that what China
possesses belongs to Japan and what China owns Japan has the
right to take.
(4) The creation of special positions on islands
along the South China coast will mean the cessation of free
trade between China and foreign countries and turn that
region into a Japanese base in the event of a war between
Japan and any European Power on the Pacific or Indian Oceans.
Secondly, the section dealing with "good
relations with neighbouring countries" contain the following
points:-
(1) Infinite rapprochement.
(2) The adoption of chain-like measures for the
whole scheme. The "chain" is tantamount to the fettering of
future generations.
The term "infinite rapprochement" is one newly
invented by Japan. Wang Ching-wei has said that he under-
stands the general outline of Prince Konoye's statement, but
does he realize that Japan is demanding "infinite rapprochement"
Wang Ching-wei's newspaper organs have shamelessly announced
that economic co-operation would be limited, but the Japanese
want "infinite rapprochement." What does the word "infinite"
mean? We have a term in Chinese meaning "boundless completeness".
Therefore the word "infinite" means "boundless" or "endless".
Apart from affiliation, there can be no rapprochement between
two sides of such a boundless or endless character. Such a
rapprochement would be nothing less than subjugation.
(3) Before Japan and Manchukuo can respect the
sovereign and territorial rights of China, the puppet regime
must first recognize Manchukuo. Can recognition of Manchukuo
State be regarded as showing respect towards the sovereign
and territorial rights of China? China does not need respect
for her sovereign and territorial rights from the puppet state
of Manchukuo, which in reality forms part of China's territory.
Is such respect mentioned by the Japanese a kind of jest or
is it to be of the nature of an insult?

1940年1月24日。下午译文。

“经济提携”一词无非是日本对中国的经济支配。这就是日本在汪精卫奴役中国之后所期望得到的。
我不愿逐一阐释协定中包含的所有苛刻条款；然而，我将处理一些更重要的要点。首先，让我们审视一些主要点：-
(1) 在“建设东亚新秩序”和“善邻友好”的理论下，旨在实现日本、中国和满洲国之间的亲善。这种亲善实现之日，即是我国独立终结之时。
(2) 提议将华北和蒙古划定为国防和经济事务紧密联合的区域，并在蒙古建立特殊的军事和政治地位。现在，我要问，这所谓的国防是指谁的国防？当中国必须在其领土内为与日本在国防事务上的合作创造特殊地位时，中国还能被称为一个独立的国家吗？
(3) 在长江下游地区建立一个密切经济合作区，仅仅意味着中国所拥有的属于日本，中国所有的东西日本有权拿走。
(4) 在华南沿海岛屿设立特殊地位，将意味着中国与外国之间自由贸易的终止，并在日本与任何欧洲强国在太平洋或印度洋发生战争时，将该地区变成日本的基地。
其次，涉及“善邻友好”的部分包含以下要点：-
(1) 无限亲善。
(2) 对整个方案采取连锁式措施。“连锁”等同于束缚子孙后代。
“无限亲善”是日本新发明的术语。汪精卫曾说，他理解近卫亲王声明的大致轮廓，但他是否意识到日本要求的是“无限亲善”？汪精卫的新闻机构无耻地宣布经济合作将是有限的，但日本人想要的是“无限亲善”。“无限”一词是什么意思？我们中文里有一个词意思是“无边的完整”。因此，“无限”一词意味着“无边”或“无尽”。除了隶属关系外，双方之间不可能存在这种无边或无尽性质的亲善。这种亲善无非就是征服。
(3) 在日本和满洲国尊重中国的主权和领土权利之前，傀儡政权必须首先承认满洲国。承认满洲国能被视为尊重中国的主权和领土权利吗？中国不需要实际上构成中国领土一部分的傀儡国家满洲国对其主权和领土权利的尊重。日本人提到的这种尊重是一种玩笑，还是一种侮辱？

January 24, 1940.

(4) The suppression of propaganda and
education as well as of political administration, commercia..
affairs and foreign policy that are detrimental to mutual
co-operation and friendship between the two countries means.
in other words, that all matters or events in China that
are regarded as unfavourable to Japan should be suppressed
(5) In her relations with third Powers, China
should adopt a policy that does not violate the fundamenta..
principles for mutual rapprochement and co-operation betwee ,
China and Japan. This is tantamount to asking China to
listen to Japan in all matters relating to China's diplomacy
in other words, it deprives China of her freedom and
independence. Does not this mean that China is to be
converted into a Japanese protectorate? Moreover, Japanese
advisors are to be employed by the new Central Government
who will be detailed to those places where strong
co-operation is necessary and to specially designated
areas. This means that Japan desires to place China
under her supervision through the medium of these advisors.
(6) Co-operation in cultural assimilation and
inventions means that China will hereafter be deprived of
her independent culture and be denied the right to make
new cultural inventions.
(7) In the measures governing the so-called
"joint defence," co-operation not only in the joint
suppression of communism but also in the joint maintenance
of peace and order is stipulated. This term "the joint
maintenance of peace and order" can only mean the conversion
of the whole of China into garrison areas for Japanese
troops, and that Japan will have the right to station
troops in any part of this country.
(8) The stationing of Japanese troops in North
China and at various strategic points in Mongolia for anti-
communist purposes; the conclusion of a military alliance
against communism; the recognition by China of Japan's
right to station warships at various specially designated
parts along the Yangtse and on various islands in South
China by the Japanese fleet --- all these places are far
away from Soviet Russia, Japan's imaginary foe, therefore
the term "anti-communism" is not applicable. For this
reason, the term "joint maintenance of peace and order"
is employed to fit the case.
According to these measures, Japan reserves
the right to secure for military purposes control of
railways, aviation, communications along leading waterways
and harbours in the areas wherein Japanese troops are
stationed, while China's military and police and defence
preparations by China are to be reduced to the minimum and
must be carried out with the co-operation of the Japanese
advisors. What does this "co-operation" mean? It is
nothing but supervision and control.
(9) Now let us examine the meaning of the so-
called economic rapprochement. It first demands mutual
guarantee and then an economic alliance. It aims at the
seizure of all the economic resources of China and the
control of her financial and economic policy as well as
her Customs tariff.

(4) 压制宣传和教育，以及压制不利于两国相互合作与友谊的政治行政、商业..事务和外交政策，换句话说，意味着应压制中国所有被视为对日本不利的事项或事件。
(5) 在与第三国的关系中，中国应采取不违反中日相互亲善与合作基本原则的政策。这等同于要求中国在涉及中国外交的所有事务上听从日本，换句话说，它剥夺了中国的自由和独立。这难道不意味着中国将被转变为日本的保护国吗？此外，新的中央政府将聘用日本顾问，他们将被派往需要强力合作的地点和特别指定的区域。这意味着日本希望通过这些顾问将中国置于其监督之下。
(6) 文化同化和发明方面的合作，意味着中国此后将被剥夺其独立文化，并被否认进行新文化发明的权利。
(7) 在所谓“共同防卫”的措施中，规定不仅在共同镇压共产主义方面进行合作，而且在共同维持治安方面也进行合作。“共同维持治安”这一术语只能意味着将整个中国变成日军的驻防区，日本将有权在这个国家的任何地方驻扎军队。
(8) 以反共为目的在华北和蒙古各战略要点驻扎日军；缔结反共军事同盟；中国承认日本舰队在中国长江沿线各特别指定部分和华南各岛屿驻扎军舰的权利——所有这些地点都远离苏联（日本假想的敌人），因此“反共”一词并不适用。出于这个原因，使用了“共同维持治安”一词以符合情况。
根据这些措施，日本保留为军事目的控制日军驻扎区域内的铁路、航空、主要水道沿线的通讯和港口的权利，而中国的军事、警察和防御准备将减少到最低限度，并且必须在日本顾问的合作下进行。这种“合作”意味着什么？它无非就是监督和控制。
(9) 现在让我们审视所谓经济提携的含义。它首先要求相互保证，然后是经济联盟。其目的是夺取中国所有的经济资源，并控制其财政和经济政策以及海关关税。

(10) As regards the matters relating to the development of China's resources, the Customs tariff, aviation, communications and meteorology, a pact is to be reached which will be entirely in accordance with the requirements of Japan.
(11) As for the development and utilization of resources, Japan will enjoy special facilities in North China and Inner Mongolia; similar facilities are to be granted to Japan in the development of special resources at other places. The so-called co-operation in the management of communications in China covers aviation facilities throughout China and the railway centres in North China, including the Lunghai Line, as well as coastal navigation and along the Yangtse and other communication facilities in North China and along the Lower Yangtse.
All this means that Japan desires to seize all that China possesses, including the control of everything that is necessary for the maintenance of the livelihood of our fellow countrymen, thereby placing them under absolute slavery.
Lest these measures should be incomplete, it was noted in the "remarks" column that a close discussion should be held with the Japanese authorities. In addition, the measures contain detailed provisions concerning the relations between the puppet Central Government on the one hand and the "Reformed Government" in Nanking, the Provisional Government in North China and the Mongolian Government on the other. The principal object of these measures is to facilitate the gradual disintegration of Chinese territory! What has attracted the close attention of the people are the paragraphs referring individually to Amoy and Hainan Island. According to these paragraphs, Amoy is to be converted into a special administrative area, while, on the other hand, Japan is to be recognized as having special rights to deal with aviation, navigation and communication facilities on the island, to develop and utilize all the special resources of the island for national defence purposes. This is tantamount to the perpetual cession of these two places to Japan.
The paragraphs also refer to certain specially designated isles along the South China coast. We should realize that all this means that Japan intends to use China to finance her adventures in the north and the south.
A study of this secret pact reveals the fact that it is far more poisonous and comprehensive than the Twenty-One Demands that were submitted to the late Yuan Shih-kai by Japan in the 4th Year (1915) of the Chinese Republic. If these humiliating terms are accepted, China will be plunged into a hopeless state, while the 450,000,000 descendants of Emperor Huang Tih will have no more hope for survival and East Asia and the world will be faced with a great calamity.
Yet Wang Ching-wei, a heartless person, gladly signed this pact on December 30 last year.
Fellow countrymen, does this pact mean peace or is it one that has sold the nation? Is it a pact that will lead to a readjustment of diplomatic relations between the two countries or is it one that contains terms humiliating to the nation? Will the enforcement of the terms stipulated in this pact assure the independence and freedom of China or will it lead to the complete deprivation of China's independence and freedom?

(To be continued)

1940年1月24日。
下午译件

(10) 关于中国资源开发、海关关税、航空、交通及气象等事项，将达成一项完全符合日本要求的协定。
(11) 在资源的开发与利用方面，日本将在华北及内蒙古享有特殊便利；在其他地方开发特种资源时，亦将给予日本类似的便利。所谓在中国交通管理方面的合作，涵盖全中国的航空设施、包括陇海线在内的华北铁路枢纽，以及沿海航运、长江沿线和华北、长江下游的其他交通设施。
这一切意味着日本企图攫取中国所有的一切，包括控制维持我国同胞生计所必需的一切，从而将他们置于绝对的奴役之下。
唯恐这些措施尚不完善，在“备注”栏中注明应与日本当局进行密切商讨。此外，这些措施还包含关于伪中央政府对一方面，与南京“维新政府”、华北“临时政府”及蒙古政府另一方面之间关系的详细规定。这些措施的主要目的是便于逐步瓦解中国领土！引起民众密切关注的，是分别提及厦门和海南岛的条款。根据这些条款，厦门将被改为特别行政区，而另一方面，日本将被承认在该岛拥有处理航空、航运及交通设施的特殊权利，并为国防目的开发和利用该岛的所有特种资源。这无异于将这两处地方永久割让给日本。
这些条款还提及华南沿海某些特别指定的岛屿。我们应认识到，这一切意味着日本打算利用中国来为其在北方和南方的冒险行动提供资金。
研究这项秘密协定可知，其毒辣和全面程度远超日本于中华民国四年（1915年）向已故袁世凯提出的“二十一条”。如果接受这些屈辱条款，中国将陷入绝望境地，而四亿五千万黄帝子孙将再无生存希望，东亚乃至世界将面临巨大灾难。
然而，无情之徒汪精卫竟于去年12月30日欣然签署了此项协定。
同胞们，这项协定意味着和平，还是卖国？它是导致两国关系调整的协定，还是包含辱国条款的协定？执行本协定规定的条款，是能保障中国的独立与自由，还是会导致中国独立与自由的彻底丧失？

（待续）

pages.en:
January 24, 1940. Afternoon Translation.

Hwa Pao and National Herald :-
WANG CHING-WEI'S FOLLOWERS ADVISED TO REPENT.
The Anti-Corruption Movement Committee of various circles in Shanghai yesterday addressed a letter to Wang Ching-wei's followers pursuading them to repent and to accept this as a last advice. The letter stated that although Wang Ching-wei had despatched a circular telegram supporting the policy of Hirota and the statement of Konoye, the people in Shanghai have paid no heed to him.
Wang Ching-wei fully understands that Japan will never give up her original policy. He intends to promote his peace movement in order to disrupt the unity of China and to lower her spirit in the war of resistance.
Recently Wang signed with Japan a pact, which is more harmful than the Twenty-one Demands, for the formation of a new puppet government. Wang's plans have been completely exposed and it is hoped that members of his organisation will quickly return to the righteous path.

National Herald and. China Evening News :-
"FORD" TAXI DRIVER ASSAULTED BY GAMBLING DEN DESPERADOES.
On January 20, a "Ford" Taxi driver was assaulted by desperadoes attached to a gambling den. This has aroused the anger of all taxi drivers in Shanghai and it is said that they will refuse to drive passengers to or from the Chiu Yuan (秋園) Gambling Den.
It appears that at about 7 p.m. January 20, some person ordered a car from the "Ford" Taxi Branch on Avenue Edward VII, near the Nanking Theatre, which is operated by Wu Su-ming (吳叔明). When the car, license No.12345, arrived at the Chiu Yuan Gambling Den, 15 Jessfield Road, the passengers instructed more than 10 desperadoes belonging to the gambling den to assault the driver who was injured about the head and the right ear. He was then locked up in a special room.
At about 10 p.m. the "Ford" Taxi Co. sent members to take the matter up with the gambling den concerned and the driver was released and taken to the Chinese Red Cross Hospital on Avenue Haig for treatment.

National Herald, Shun Pao, Central-China Daily News, Sin Wan Pao, Chinese-American Daily News, Sze Tei Wan Pao and Sin Wan Pao (Evening Edition) :-
LOCAL HOT-WATER SHOPS
Yesterday Chang Teh-lung (張德龍) and Yu Lien-fah (俞蓮法), Chairman and Vice-Chairman respectively of the Shanghai Municipality Hot Water Shop-keepers Guild, handed to Messrs. Yu Ya-ching (虞洽卿), Yuan Lu-tung (袁履登) and Kwei Ting-fang (桂廷芳) the following petition asking for their assistance.
pages.zh:
1940年1月24日。下午译件。

《华报》与《国民日报》：
劝告汪精卫追随者悔悟。
上海各界反贪腐运动委员会昨日致函汪精卫追随者，劝其悔悟，并以此作为最后忠告。信中指出，尽管汪精卫发出支持广田政策及近卫声明的通电，但上海民众对其置之不理。
汪精卫充分明白日本绝不会放弃其原有政策。他意图推动其和平运动，以破坏中国团结，降低抗战士气。
近日，汪精卫与日本签订了一项比“二十一条”危害更甚的协定，以组建新的傀儡政府。汪的计划已完全暴露，希望其组织成员迅速回归正途。

《国民日报》及《中国晚报》：
“福特”出租车司机遭赌窟暴徒殴打。
1月20日，一名“福特”出租车司机遭赌窟暴徒殴打。此事激起上海所有出租车司机的愤怒，据悉他们将拒绝载客往返秋园赌场。
据悉，1月20日晚7时许，有人向位于南京大戏院附近爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）、由吴叔明经营的“福特”出租车分行叫车。当车牌号为12345的车辆抵达杰斯菲尔德路15号（15 Jessfield Road）的秋园赌场时，乘客指令赌场十余名暴徒殴打司机，致其头部及右耳受伤。随后司机被锁入一间特设房间内。
晚10时许，“福特”出租车公司派人前往涉事赌场交涉，司机获释并被送往海格路（Avenue Haig）中国红十字会医院接受治疗。

《国民日报》、《申报》、《华中日报》、《新闻报》、《中美日报》、《四德晚报》及《新闻报》（晚刊）：
本地热水店业者
昨日，上海市热水店同业公会主席张德龙及副主席俞莲法，向虞洽卿、袁履登及桂廷芳三位先生递交下列请愿书，请求协助。

pages.en:
January 24, 1940. Afternoon Translation.

(1) To write to the Kailan Mining Administration asking
it to sell coal to hot-water shops at a fixed price.
(2) To urge various trade circles to make a joint
purchase of coal from outports and to keep sufficient
stocks of coal in Shanghai to meet . demands.
(3) To request local coal dealers to sell their stocks
at a fixed price, so that sufficient stocks may be
obtained and the price may be brought to its proper
level.
The above three gentlemen
promised their assistance in the matter, as they are in
sympathy with the hot-water shops.

Shun Pao and Ta Mei Pao :-

A FAMOUS GERMAN DOCTOR TAKES OUT CHINESE NATURALIZATION
PAPER

Dr. William Rosenberg, a famous German
doctor, residing at 934 Bubbling Well Road, has been in
China for over six years, in the course of which he made
an investigation into China's culture. He likes to
associate with Chinese people and he has expressed himself
as being in sympathy with the Chinese people in the war of
resistance. He has rendered meritorious service by
attending to wounded Chinese soldiers and civilians.
Recently he renounced his German
nationality and took out Chinese naturalization papers
after approval had been secured from the Ministry of
Interior of the National Government. His naturalization
paper, No.3062, was issued on December 21, 1939.

Sin Wan Pao:-

DETECTIVE ABDUCTED FROM AN OPIUM DEN

At 8.20 p.m. January 22, six or seven
nationals of a certain country, armed with Mauser pistols,
searched the Sin Ying Gambling Den (信行賭場) at Brenan
Piece in the Western District. The party subsequently
entered an opium smoking den next door and carried away
a pock-marked male Chinese of about 30 years of age who
speaks the northern dialect. Despite a desperate struggle
put up by the man, he was taken away in the direction of
Connaught Road.
According to an unconfirmed report,
the man, whose surname is Chang (張), is a detective
sergeant attached to a certain police station.

Hwa Mei Wan Pao of January 23 :-

OPEN LETTER TO YOUTHS RECEIVED BY NEWSPAPER

This morning this paper received a
letter signed by the "China Revolutionary Youth League"
(中華革命青年團) enclosing a mimeographed draft of an
article entitled "Open letter to youths in Shanghai
revealing intrigues" in which the plans of Wang Ching-wei
to barter away the nation were dealt at length and youths
were exhorted not to be utilized by the Wang Ching-wei
clique.
pages.zh:
1940年1月24日。下午译件。

(1) 致函开滦矿务总局，要求其以固定价格向热水店出售煤炭。
(2) 敦促各商界联合从外埠采购煤炭，并在上海保持充足库存以满足需求。
(3) 请求本地煤商以固定价格出售库存，以便获得充足存货并使价格回归合理水平。
上述三位先生表示同情热水店业者，承诺在此事上提供协助。

《申报》及《大美报》：
著名德籍医生加入中国国籍

威廉·罗森伯格（William Rosenberg）博士是一位著名的德籍医生，居住于静安寺路934号，在华已逾六年，期间对中国文化进行了考察。他乐于与中国人交往，并表示同情中国人民的抗战。他在救治中国伤兵及平民方面做出了贡献。
近日，他放弃德国国籍，在获得国民政府内政部批准后，取得了中国入籍证书。其入籍证书编号为3062，签发日期为1939年12月21日。

《新闻报》：
侦探自鸦片馆被绑架

1月22日晚8时20分，六七名某国籍人士手持毛瑟手枪，搜查西区布伦南片（Brenan Piece）的信行赌场。随后，该伙人进入隔壁的一家鸦片烟馆，带走一名约30岁、讲北方方言、面部有麻点的中国男子。尽管该男子拼命挣扎，仍被带往康纳脱路（Connaught Road）方向。
据未经证实的消息称，该男子姓张，系某警察局的侦探巡长。

1月23日《华美晚报》：
报社收到致青年公开信

今晨本报收到一封署名为“中华革命青年团”的信件，附有一份题为《揭露阴谋致上海青年公开信》的油印稿草案，文中详细论述了汪精卫出卖国家的计划，并告诫青年不要受汪精卫集团利用。

pages.en:
January 24, 1940.
Afternoon Translation.

Chinese-American Daily News, Ta Mei Pao, Sin Wan Pao, National
Herald, Shun Pao :-

IRON GATES IN NANTAO TO BE RE-OPENED

In November last year, the Japanese authorities
re-opened some of the iron gates on the border of the
French Concession and Nantao. People in possession of
passes issued in October and December were refused admittance
into Nantao.
According to information secured yesterday by
a reporter of the Dah Tung News Agency, the Japanese
authorities, in the name of the Commander of the Japanese
Army in Central China, posted up a notice in Nantao on
January 23, stating that all iron gates east of Jih Huei Kong
(日暉港) in Nantao will be re-opened on January 24 and
people in possession of citizens' certificates issued by
the Shanghai City Government will be allowed to return to
Nantao.
For this reason, the iron gates at Small North
Gate, Old North Gate, New North Gate, south end of
Boulevard de Montigny and other places in Nantao will be
re-opened to-day.

National Herald, Sin Wan Pao, Ta Ying Yeh Pao :-

CHINESE DETECTIVE DEPRIVED OF SERVICE PISTOL

(金德順), At 1.15 p.m. yesterday, while Chin Tuh-zung
a detective No. 136 of the Settlement Police
Station, was passing the corner of Hart and Connaught Roads
in the Western District, two highway robbers jumped out
from the roadside, drew their pistols and held him up.
Taken by surprise, the detective was unable to offer any
resistance and was robbed of his service pistol (No.1697),
14 rounds of ammunition and $20 in legal tender notes.
The robbers made good their escape.
A report was made by the detective to the
Police Station concerned.

Ta Mei Wan Pao (23/1) :-

FRENCH TRAMWAY MECHANICS ASK FOR DOUBLE PAY

Yesterday afternoon the mechanics of the
Compagnie Française de Tramways et d'Eclairage Electriques
de Shanghai went on a "go-slow" strike for a short time
when they failed to get a satisfactory reply to their demand
for double pay.
Subsequently responsible officials of the
company offered to mediate and promised to consider the
workers' demand and to give a reply on the afternoon of
January 23. Upon learning of this, the strikers resumed
work.
pages.zh:
1940年1月24日。
下午译件。

《中美日报》、《大美报》、《新闻报》、《国民日报》、《申报》：

南市铁门将重新开放

去年11月，日本当局重新开放了法租界与南市边界的部分铁门。持有10月和12月签发通行证的人员被拒绝进入南市。
据大通社记者昨日获悉的消息，日本当局以华中日军司令的名义，于1月23日在南市张贴告示，称南市日晖港以东的所有铁门将于1月24日重新开放，持有上海市政府签发的市民证的人员将被允许返回南市。
因此，南市的小北门、老北门、新北门、蒙塔尼路（Boulevard de Montigny）南端及其他地方的铁门将于今日重新开放。

《国民日报》、《新闻报》、《大英夜报》：

华籍侦探被缴去佩枪

金德顺，昨日午后1时15分，公共租界捕房第136号侦探金德顺（Chin Tuh-zung）在西区哈特路（Hart Road）与康纳脱路拐角处经过时，两名路劫匪从路边跳出，拔出手枪将其拦住。侦探猝不及防，无法抵抗，被抢去佩枪（编号1697）、子弹14发及法币20元。劫匪随即逃逸。
该侦探已向相关捕房报案。

1月23日《大美晚报》：

法商电车机匠要求双倍工资

昨日下午，上海法商电车电灯公司（Compagnie Française de Tramways et d'Eclairage Electriques de Shanghai）的机匠因要求双倍工资未获满意答复，进行了短时间的“怠工”罢工。
随后，公司负责官员提出调解，承诺考虑工人要求，并于1月23日下午给予答复。罢工者得知此消息后复工。

pages.en:
January 24, 1940. Afternoon Translation.

Shun Pao (letter from Soochow) :-

JAPANESE MERCHANTS BUYING 30,000 PICULS OF RICE IN SOOCHOW

The Japanese Special Service Section in
Soochow, at the request of Japanese merchants, has ordered
the puppet hsien governments of Soochow and Wukiang to
purchase 30,000 piculs of rice at Yen 27 per picul.
Koh Tseng-chien ( 新曾建 ) and Tsu Yuan-chih
( 朱之直 ), the puppet magistrates of Soochow and Wukiang
respectively, have been holding conferences with rice
merchants since January 15, with the result that rice
merchants have requested every village to sell 1,000
piculs of rice each in order to please the Japanese
authorities.
pages.zh:
1940年1月24日。下午译件。

《申报》（苏州来信）：

日商在苏州购买三万担大米

苏州日本特务机关应日商请求，命令苏州及吴江伪县政府以每担27日元的价格购买大米三万担。
苏州及吴江伪县长葛曾建（音译，原文为 Koh Tseng-chien / 新曾建）与朱之直自1月15日起一直与米商开会协商，结果是米商为讨好日本当局，要求每个村庄各出售一千担大米。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. 5, Special Branch
REPORT
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / SPECIAL BRANCH REGISTRY / No. S. B. D. 1590/1 / Date December 22, 1930）
Subject. Objectionable advertisement appearing in the "Hwa Pao"
Made by....................and....................Forwarded by....D.S.I. Golder.

Acting on instructions received from P.A.
to D.C. (Special Branch), the managements of the "Sin
Wan Pao," the "Shun Pao," the "Ta Mei Pao," the
"Chinese-American Daily News," the"Hwa Pao," the "China
Evening News," the "Ta Mei Wan Pao," the "Hwa Mei Wan
Pao," etc., were requested to refrain from accepting
advertisements for insertion in their respective papers
from the employees of the Sincere Company relating to
their recent strike.
As Mr. H.P. Mills, publisher of the "Hwa
Pao" and "Hwa Mei Wan Pao," was not in the office,
Mr. Chu Tso-dong (朱作栋), general manager of the two
papers, was communicated with and agreed to act as
requested. However, in to-day's issue of the "Hwa Pao,"
the advertisement which was contained in December 21st
issue of the "National Herald" (translation attached)
was reproduced in the advertisement column.
Upon being asked, Chu Tso-dong explained on
December 22 that the failure of his paper in observing
the request of the Police is due to one of his employees
who had omitted to carry out his instructions.
Mr. Mills was communicated with this
afternoon when he expressed regret for failure to comply
with the request of Police in this connection and stated
that no negligence of this nature would be allowed in future.

经询问，朱作栋于12月22日解释说，其报纸未能遵守警方要求，是由于一名雇员未执行他的指令所致。
今天下午与 Mills 先生取得了联系，他对未能遵从此项警方要求表示遗憾，并表示今后绝不允许发生此类疏忽。

December 21, 1939. Morning Translation.

OPEN LETTER ADDRESSED TO THE PUBLIC BY THE EMPLOYEES
OF THE SINCERE COMPANY

The employees of the Sincere Company publish
the following open letter addressed to the public in the
advertising columns of the "National Herald" to-day:-
In these days of high living costs in this
isolated city of Shanghai, people of the salary class have
found it difficult to maintain themselves and have
submitted demands to their employers for better treatment.
We, employees of the Sincere Company, are no
exception. On December 10, we declared a "go-slow"
strike, but through the mediation of Messrs Koo Ping-yuan
(顧炳元) and Kao Yen-keng (高嚴根) of the S.M.C. and out
of consideration of the present difficult situation, we
resumed work pending a favourable reply from our employers.
On December 18, a telegraphic reply was received
from the head office in Hongkong, and contending that the
employers had not yet fully understood the circumstances,
we on the afternoon of December 19 appointed representatives
to call on Mr. Cheng Chao-ping (鄭超平), the manager, who
has now given us the following reply:-
1) As from this month, the employees will be given a
monthly rice allowance of $3 each.
2) The original bonus equivalent to three days' pay will be
hereafter granted as a permanent allowance. Another
bonus of three days' pay now demanded will be called a
provisional allowance and will come into effect as from
January 1 next year.
3) As regards the protection of our employment, the
management will not dismiss any worker unless verbal
warnings have been given him. The number of warnings,
however, is not certain.
4) Measures will be devised in connection with the issue of
annual bonus to the employees. A definite reply in this
respect will be given to the employees before the end of
the year. The management will not disappoint the
employees.
To secure co-operation between the capital and
labour, and knowing that protection of the company means
the preservation of our livelihood, we have regarded for
the time being the above reply as satisfactory, but a
full settlement of the dispute has not yet been effected.
We are deeply appreciative of the help from
various people. We hereby publish the above particulars
for public information.

1939年12月21日。上午译文。

先施公司职员致公众的公开信

先施公司职员今日在《国民新闻报》的广告栏中刊登以下致公众的公开信：
在这个生活成本高昂的上海孤岛时期，薪金阶层人士发现难以维持生计，并向雇主提出了改善待遇的要求。
我们，先施公司的职员，也不例外。12月10日，我们宣布实行“怠工”罢工，但经过工部局顾炳元（Koo Ping-yuan）和高严根（Kao Yen-keng）两位先生的调解，并考虑到当前的困难局势，我们在等待雇主有利答复的同时恢复了工作。
12月18日，收到香港总公司的电报回复，鉴于雇主尚未完全了解情况，我们于12月19日下午指派代表拜访经理郑超平（Cheng Chao-ping）先生，他现在给予我们如下答复：
1) 从本月起，每位职员每月将获得3元的大米津贴。
2) 原相当于三天薪水的奖金将此后作为永久津贴发放。目前要求的另一笔相当于三天薪水的奖金将称为临时津贴，并从明年1月1日起生效。
3) 关于保障我们的就业问题，管理层不会解雇任何工人，除非已对其发出口头警告。但是，警告的次数并不确定。
4) 将制定有关向职员发放年终奖金的措施。在此方面将在年底前给予职员明确答复。管理层不会让职员失望。
为了争取资方与劳方的合作，并深知保护公司即意味着保全我们的生计，我们暂时认为上述答复令人满意，但纠纷尚未得到全面解决。
我们对各界人士的帮助深表感激。特此公布上述详情，以供公众知悉。

NOV 28 1939
Hwa Pao 1-NOV 28 1939 A.M.
BLOOD
Blood is being shed in every corner of the country.
Are the people of China willing to become slaves?
Splash the hot blood on our own territory.
Why should we hesitate?
The insult and humiliation to our people must be wiped
out at one time,
While the enmity of a century should be liquidated
at the same time.
People under heavy oppression are shouting:
"Shed blood for the sake of our existence!"
We need not care if the land is so red that the sun
is afraid, or if the blood becomes a great torrent.
We should tell them that we are not tame sheep to be
placed at the disposal of others.
We must realize that our blood will not be wasted in
vain,
And the blood that has been shed during the past 29
months has produced the sprout of victory.

1939年11月28日
华报 1-1939年11月28日 上午
血
国土每一个角落都在流血。
中国人民愿意做奴隶吗？
把热血洒在我们自己的领土上。
我们何必犹豫？
必须一次性洗雪对我们人民的侮辱和耻辱，
同时清算百年的仇恨。
受重压下的人民在呐喊：
“为了生存而流血！”
我们不必在乎土地是否红得让太阳害怕，或者血液是否变成巨大的洪流。
我们要告诉他们，我们不是任人摆布的温顺绵羊。
我们必须认识到，我们的血不会白流，
过去29个月所流的血已经孕育出胜利的萌芽。

June 19, 1939. Morning Translation.

Hwa Pao (Editorial) of June 18 :-

THE QUESTION OF THE SAFETY OF THE FOREIGN SETTLEMENTS
IN SHANGHAI

Are the Foreign Settlements in Shanghai safe?
To obtain a reply to this question, we have
first to study the following points:-
We should examine the circumstances that
had brought about the blockade of the British and French
Concessions in Tientsin and the International Settlement
at Kulangsu. We know that the Tientsin blockade is only
a preliminary step towards the seizure of the rights and
interests of Britain, France and other Powers. If this
step proves successful, Japan will become more aggressive;
in that event the safety of the Foreign Settlements in
Shanghai will be in doubt.
Will the blockade succeed? What does Japan
expect to derive from the blockade?
According to a Reuter's telegram from Tokyo
dated June 16, Japan will not lift the blockade until
the British accept the following four conditions:-
(1) Joint search for terroristic elements.
(2) Suppression of anti-Japanese elements.
(3) No further meddling with the economic
arrangements made by the Provisional Government in North
China.
(4) The handing over of the $50,000,000
in silver in the reserve of the Chinese banks.
Will the authorities of the British Concession
accept these demands? They are not in a position to comply
with these demands. It is not because of their regard for
Chinese rights and interests or for the purpose of
protecting the Chinese patriotic elements that the British
will reject these demands, but because they realize that
once the demands are accepted, Japan may resort to similar
steps to enforce further demands on Britain and soon
Britain will lose all her interests in the Far East. That
this surmise is not absolutely groundless is proved by
the fact that Japan had at first demanded only the
extradition of the four patriotic Chinese elements, but
afterwards the number of demands increased as if Japan
was determined to push on with her demands until the
withdrawal of the British Consul in Tientsin. Whether or
not Britain will be able to safeguard her interests in
the Far East will depend upon her attitude in the present
affair. We know that Britain will never abandon her
interests in the Orient for the British residents in Tientsin
have been ordered to remain calm and patient. We should
not mistake patience for submissiveness. We believe that
the British Residents will not bow to force.
So far as the present conditions are
concerned, the following are the serious problems that are
now confronting the British Concession authorities in
Tientsin:-
(1) The increasing activities of the agitators
and instigators.

FILE

1939年6月19日。晨间译件。

6月18日《华报》（社论）：-

上海外国租界的安全问题

上海的外国租界安全吗？
要回答这个问题，我们首先必须研究以下几点：-
我们应该考察导致天津英法租界和鼓浪屿公共租界被封锁的情况。我们知道，天津封锁只是夺取英国、法国及其他列强权利和利益的初步步骤。如果这一步骤成功，日本将变得更加咄咄逼人；在这种情况下，上海外国租界的安全将令人担忧。
封锁会成功吗？日本期望从封锁中获得什么？
根据6月16日从东京发出的路透社电报，在日本接受以下四个条件之前，日本不会解除封锁：-
(1) 联合搜查恐怖分子。
(2) 镇压反日分子。
(3) 不再干涉华北临时政府做出的经济安排。
(4) 移交中国银行储备中的5,000万美元白银。
英租界当局会接受这些要求吗？他们无法遵守这些要求。英国拒绝这些要求，并非出于对中国权利和利益的尊重，或为了保护中国爱国分子，而是因为他们意识到，一旦接受这些要求，日本可能会采取类似手段迫使英国接受进一步的要求，很快英国将失去其在远东的所有利益。这种推测并非毫无根据，事实证明，日本起初仅要求引渡四名中国爱国分子，但随后要求的数量增加，仿佛日本决心不断推进其要求，直至英国驻天津领事撤离。英国能否保卫其在远东的利益，将取决于其在此事上的态度。我们知道，英国绝不会为了在天津的英国居民而放弃其在东方的利益，因为这些居民已被命令保持冷静和耐心。我们不应将耐心误认为顺从。我们相信，英国居民不会向武力低头。
就目前的状况而言，以下是天津英租界当局现在面临的严重问题：-
(1) 煽动者和挑拨者的活动日益增加。

档案

pages.en:
(2) The continued shortage of foodstuffs.
(3) The proposed visit to Japanese graves by
Japanese residents and reserves.
However, we believe that so long as the
British residents remain calm and patient, the blockade
will not have any serious effect. This does not mean that
patience will create a kind of mysterious force which will
break the blockade. When we study the Far Eastern
situation, we should pay attention to the developments
in Europe; the two are closely connected with each other.
Soviet Russia is willing to join the Anglo-
French military pact in order to assist Britain and France
in dealing with the European situation, but the views
held by Britain and Soviet Russia are widely different
Still we believe that a military pact by these three nations
will be signed, for they have to unite for the sake of their
own interests.
Sometime ago, the British Conservative Party
suggested the holding of a round table conference in the
hope of continuing negotiations with Germany and Italy.
On the surface this might appear a slight upon Soviet
Russia, but in reality, it indicates the eagerness of
Britain to come to an understanding with Soviet Russia.
One thing must be noted when the problem
of the safety of Shanghai is considered. Although Japan
is taking action against Britain and France, she has no
intention at present to provoke America. American
steamers have never been searched by the Japanese and
prior to the blockade of the British Concession in Tientsin,
Japan sent a note to the American Consul in Tientsin asking
for his understanding of the measure. This is clear proof
that Japan has no intention at present to provoke America.
Japan has made certain concessions in the Kulengsu affair
simply because America is involved in the case.
Britain is the leading Power in the
International Settlement of Shanghai, but America has
also interests in the city. Japan will have to pay
attention to this point in case she desires to take action
against the International Settlement. This is one of the
reasons why we hold the view that there will be no danger
for the safety of the Foreign Settlements of Shanghai for
the time being.
pages.zh:
(2) 食品持续短缺。
(3) 日本居民和后备役人员提议参拜日本墓地。
然而，我们认为，只要英国居民保持冷静和耐心，封锁就不会产生任何严重影响。这并不意味着耐心会产生一种打破封锁的神秘力量。当我们研究远东局势时，应关注欧洲的事态发展；两者密切相关。
苏联愿意加入英法军事协定，以协助英法应对欧洲局势，但英国和苏联的观点大相径庭。尽管如此，我们相信这三个国家将签署一项军事协定，因为它们必须为了自身利益而团结。
不久前，英国保守党建议举行圆桌会议，希望继续与德国和意大利进行谈判。表面上看，这似乎是对苏联的轻视，但实际上，这表明英国渴望与苏联达成谅解。
在考虑上海安全问题时，有一点必须注意。虽然日本正在对英国和法国采取行动，但目前无意挑衅美国。日本从未搜查过美国轮船，且在天津英租界被封锁之前，日本曾向美国驻天津领事发出照会，请求其理解这一措施。这清楚地证明，日本目前无意挑衅美国。日本在鼓浪屿事件中做出某些让步，仅仅是因为美国卷入其中。
英国是上海公共租界的主要列强，但美国在该市也有利益。如果日本希望对公共租界采取行动，就必须注意这一点。这也是我们认为上海外国租界的安全暂时不会有危险的原因之一。

REPORT    149.C491
Date July 9. 1939.7.9

Subject Untrue report of search of French Concession hotels by Japanese.

Made by and Forwarded by D.S. Pharazyn.

With reference to the attached translation of a
report entitled "Japanese Search French Concession Hotels"
published by the "Hwa Pao" (華報) on July 4, the management of
the paper was informed that there is no truth in the report and
that a correction was required.
On July 9, the "Hwa Pao" publishes the following
correction :-

CORRECTION
On July 4, this paper published a report to
the effect that three Japanese in plain clothes had
made an inspection in the Dah Woo Hotel and had later
called at the Tung Man Lodging House and interrogated
occupants.
It has now been found that the above report is
entirely unfounded.

FILE Certificates Received M.D. Pharazyn.
July 19th 1939. in file S.D.D. S.
D. C. (Special Branch)

of July 4, 1939
Made by D.S. Pitts Forwarded by C. Gafga. S.I.

According to the French Police, there is
no truth in the attached report appearing in the
Hwa Pao of July 4, 1939 insofar as "three Japanese
in plain clothes" are concerned.
The hotels were visited, however, by
Chinese loafers at the time mentioned, they
claiming to be French Police detectives. They
remained on the premises of each hotel for not
more than two minutes, apparently being frightened
of being arrested for illegal functioning.

D.S. Pitts

July 4, 1939.
Afternoon Translation.

Hwa Pao :-

JAPANESE SEARCH FRENCH CONCESSION HOTELS

At about 10 last night, three Japanese in plain
clothes arrived at Avenue Edward VII in a motor car bearing
a special white license plate, and made an inspection in the
Dah Woo Hotel (大沪飯店). Later, they called at the
Tung Nan Lodging House (东南旅館) on Rue des Peres and
entered room 62. After interrogating the occupants of the
room, they left the place without making any arrests. No
French Police officers were present at the time when the
Japanese were carrying out their activities.

DS. Pik Please get explanation
Cky

1939年7月4日。
下午译件。

《华报》：-

日本人搜查法租界旅馆

昨晚10点左右，三名便衣日本人乘坐一辆挂有特殊白色牌照的汽车到达爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII），并对大沪饭店进行了检查。随后，他们前往神父路（Rue des Peres）的东南旅馆，进入62号房间。在审问房间住客后，他们未做任何逮捕便离开了现场。日本人进行活动时，现场没有法国警官在场。

June 1, 1939. Morning Translation.

A NEW PAPER CALLED "HWA PAO" TO BE PUBLISHED

The Hwa Mei Publishing Company, an American concern, publishes in the advertisement columns of the "Sin Wan Pao" and "Shun Pao" of to-day and the "Ta Loi Wan Pao" of May 31 the following notice announcing the publication of a new journal to be known as the "Hwa Pao" (華報) :-

"Since its establishment, this company has always worked for an improvement in Sino-American relations and has always upheld justice and righteousness. The company publishes the 'Hwa Mei Wan Pao,' the 'Hwa Mei Chen Pao,' the 'Hwa Mei Weekly' and various other magazines and books. It has always adopted a strict and fair attitude as a third party.

"On the third anniversary of this company and with a view to extending its business, we will start another daily to be called the 'Hwa Pao.' This paper will make its formal appearance on June 1. The new paper will be under strict editorial supervision so as to make its reports reliable.

"This notice is published for the information of the public."

JCSB.
file attached.

1939年6月1日。晨间译件。

一份名为《华报》的新报纸即将出版

华美出版公司（一家美国企业）在今日的《新闻报》和《申报》以及5月31日的《大罗晚报》的广告栏中刊登了以下通知，宣布出版一份名为《华报》的新期刊：-

“本公司自成立以来，一直致力于改善中美关系，始终 uphold 正义和公理。本公司出版《华美晚报》、《华美晨报》、《华美周刊》及各种其他杂志和书籍。作为第三方，本公司始终采取严格和公正的态度。

“值此本公司成立三周年之际，并为扩展业务，我们将创办另一份日报，名为《华报》。该报将于6月1日正式发行。新报将受到严格的编辑监督，以确保其报道可靠。

“特此公告，以飨公众。”

JCSB.

Reg. No. C/ 25057-8 Stn. Alnzu. Procurator Y 449 Judge Tnoong.

Accused
1. Choo Kwei Sung Age 75. Master Printer.
2. Au Chien Cheu Editor-publisher.

Charge
1st accused
Indecent publication. Contr.to Art. 235 Sec. 2 of Cr. and rt.s
22 and 34 of Press Law.
For that he, being the proprietor of the Sing Ling Printing
Works, 64 Kuling Rd, did on 24.12.40, print an indecent
advertisement in a mosquito paper known as the "El Pao".

2nd accused
Indecent publication.
For that he, on 24/12/39 at 64 Kuling Rd, being the editor-
publisher of a mosquito paper known as "El Pao" did allow to
be published an indecent advertisement.

In DISTRICT COURT No 2 (.....)
Mr. Leong appeared for the Prosecution.

Proceedings
Mr. Leong :- The accused are charged under Art. 235 of the
C.C.C. and Arts 22 and 34 of Press Law. The 1st accused is
the proprietor of the Sing Ling Printing Works, 64 Kuling Road.
He printed an indecent advertisement in a mosquito paper known
as the "El Pao", of which the 2nd accused is the publisher and
editor, on the 24/12/39. The 2nd accused is therefore also
charged under Art. 235 of the C.C.C. and Arts 22 & 34 of Press
Law. On the 24/12/39 he published an indecent article in
the said paper. He lives also in House 64 Kulin Road. He has
failed to come here to-day.

Judge to the 1st accused :-
Q. Did you publish an indecent advertisement in "El Pao" on
the 24/12/39 ?
A. Yes, I did it through negligence.

Decision
1st : Fined $30.00 or 30 days labour for assisting in publishing
indecent literature.
2nd : Fined $30 or 30 days labour for publishing indecent li-
terature.
2 newspapers to be kept on file.
1st accused : Sentence to be executed immediately.

登记号 C/ 25057-8 警局 Alnzu. 检察官 Y 449 法官 Tnoong.

被告
1. Choo Kwei Sung 年龄 75岁。印刷厂主。
2. Au Chien Cheu 编辑兼出版人。

指控
第一被告
发布淫秽出版物。违反《刑法》第235条第2款及《新闻法》第22和34条。
因其作为位于古林路64号（Kuling Rd）的兴灵印刷所（Sing Ling Printing Works）业主，于1940年12月24日在一份名为《El Pao》的小报上印制了一则淫秽广告。

第二被告
发布淫秽出版物。
因其于1939年12月24日在古林路64号，作为一份名为《El Pao》的小报的编辑兼出版人，允许刊登一则淫秽广告。

在第二特区法院 (.....)
梁先生（Mr. Leong）代表公诉方出庭。

诉讼程序
梁先生：- 被告被控违反《中华民国刑法》第235条及《新闻法》第22和34条。第一被告是位于古林路64号的兴灵印刷所的业主。他于1939年12月24日在一份名为《El Pao》的小报上印制了一则淫秽广告，该报由第二被告担任出版人和编辑。因此，第二被告也被控违反《中华民国刑法》第235条及《新闻法》第22和34条。他于1939年12月24日在该报上发表了一篇淫秽文章。他也住在古林路64号。他今天未能到庭。

法官问第一被告：-
问：你于1939年12月24日在《El Pao》上发布了淫秽广告吗？
答：是的，我是因疏忽而为之。

判决
第一被告：罚款30.00美元或服劳役30天，罪名是协助发布淫秽刊物。
第二被告：罚款30美元或服劳役30天，罪名是发布淫秽刊物。
两份报纸存档备查。
第一被告：判决立即执行。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY

Special Branch Station
REPORT Date Jan. 10, 1940.

Subject Indecent advertisement appearing in Wei Pao on December 24,
1939.

Made by D.S. Pharazyn Forwarded by En. Golan. D.I.

Further to the attached report, Mr. Thomas S.
Lea, acting Municipal Advocate, who was consulted on
January 8 in connection with the advertisement
appearing in the Wei Pao (彙報), a Chinese mosquito
paper, on December 24, 1939, was of opinion that the
insertion was indecent and that the Police were
justified in taking action against the editor and the
printer of the paper under Article 235 Section 1 and 2
of the Chinese Criminal Code and Articles 22 and 34 of
the Press Law.

Submitted for favour of signature by D. C.
(Special Branch) are applications for Summons against
Zau Chien-cheu (趙鑑秋), the editor-publisher, and
Chow Kwei-sung (周桂生), the proprietor of the Sing
Sing Printing Works (新印刷所), 64 Kuling Road,
which undertakes the printing of the paper.

Enquiries made by C.D.C. 230 Chang Yeh show
that the paper in question has been out of publication
since January 3, but according to Zau Chien-cheu,
the paper will soon resume publication.

The attached translations of an advertisement,
inserted by the aforementioned drug store, which are of
a slight difference in text, are taken from the Sin Wan
Pao and the China Evening News of January 8, the Social
Daily News (社會日報) and the Shanghai Daily News
(上海日報) of January 6 and the Tao Sheh Sin Wan Pao
(桃色新聞報) of January 7.

D. C. (Special Branch).

（左侧批注：X Signed by D.C. sp.
& sent to Cav.
Jan 21）

主题 1939年12月24日出现在《彙報》上的淫秽广告。

制作人 D.S. Pharazyn 转发人 En. Golan. D.I.

继附件报告之后，代理市公署律师 Thomas S. Lea 先生于1月8日就1939年12月24日出现在中文小报《彙報》（Wei Pao）上的广告一事接受咨询，他认为该插入内容属淫秽性质，警方有理由根据《中华民国刑法》第235条第1和第2款以及《新闻法》第22和34条对该报的编辑和印刷商采取行动。

呈请特务科副督察长（D. C.）签署针对编辑兼出版人赵鉴秋（Zau Chien-cheu，趙鑑秋）以及承担该报印刷业务的古林路64号新印刷所（Sing Sing Printing Works，原文误作新印刷所，前文为新新印刷所）业主周桂生（Chow Kwei-sung，周桂生）的传票申请。

华籍侦探警长（C.D.C.）230号张叶（Chang Yeh）经查询显示，涉案报纸自1月3日起已停刊，但据赵鉴秋称，该报即将复刊。

特务科副督察长（D. C.）。

并送至 Cav.
1月21日）

REPORT
Date December 4, 1939.

Subject (in full) Mosquito paper editor and printer fined for publishing
indecent articles

Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Golder.

Further to the attached report dated November 16
and in connection with the case against Yu Jen-ying
(俞人英), editor of a mosquito paper known as "Wei Pao"
(彙報), and Chow Kwei-sung (周桂生), proprietor of
the Sing Sing Printing Works (新新印刷所), 64 Kuling Road,
for the publication and printing of two indecent articles
which appeared in the paper on November 6, summonses were
served on the two accused on the morning of November 22.
On November 27 the case was heard at the Shanghai First
Special District Court but neither of the two accused
appeared in person. Consequently the case was remanded
to December 4, 1939.

On December 4 the case came up on remand when
Yu Jen-ying, the editor, who was represented by Zau Chien-
cheu (趙鑑秋), the publisher of the mosquito paper in
question, was fined $40, while Chow Kwei-sung, proprietor
of the printing works, was fined $20. Both fines are
convertible to a term of detention at the rate of $1 one
day.

D. C. (Special Branch).

Em Golder
D. S. I.
